headline: Low prompt-injection and data-leakage risk; no shared surfaces are documented, but A’s broad egress warrants caution.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel, filesystem, or parser bridge is documented for either agent, so a prompt-injection pathway is not evidenced. A is content-writing with broad network egress, while B is data-engineering with no egress, but neither profile shows ingestion of the other’s outputs by default.
conditions: IF a shared clipboard, filesystem, or MCP bridge is added between the agents, injection risk becomes plausible.
IF either agent begins parsing the other’s raw text as instructions, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable any shared clipboard or message queue.
Require explicit human copy-paste between agents.
Add provenance labels to any transferred text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both profiles touch no data classes and expose no shared workspace, so leakage is not documented. However, A has broad network egress while B has none, and if sensitive content were introduced into A, its outbound path could leak it; the pairwise interaction is undocumented, so uncertainty keeps this above none.
conditions: IF sensitive data is placed into A’s context and A is allowed to transmit it, leakage risk increases.
IF a shared workspace is later introduced, reassess upward.
mitigations: Do not place secrets in either agent’s prompts.
Keep network access disabled for A when handling sensitive material.
Use separate local workspaces.
Review outbound destinations before enabling egress.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write surfaces, OAuth scopes, databases, or filesystem permissions are documented for either agent. A’s broad egress and B’s no-egress posture do not create a write conflict by themselves, so the capability-conflict pathway is not supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same mutable resource, conflict risk becomes plausible.
IF an orchestrator adds shared locking-free state, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep mutable resources out of both agents’ scope.
Avoid granting shared OAuth scopes.
Use separate repositories or directories.
Add locking if shared state is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Neither profile shows downstream action-taking authority, and no evidence indicates that B treats A’s output as authoritative. A is a content-writing agent and B is data-engineering, but without a documented handoff or verification gap, a cascading-error pathway is not established.
conditions: IF B is configured to execute actions directly from A’s text, reassess upward.
IF A’s outputs are later used as authoritative facts without verification, cascading error becomes plausible.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Require source citations before B acts on A’s output.
Restrict B to read-only evaluation of A’s text.
Log handoffs for auditability.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either agent, and both profiles list empty data_classes_touched. With no evidence of PHI, EU PII, or retention mismatch, a compliance breach pathway is not supported.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into either agent, reassess against the relevant residency and retention rules.
IF one agent is later certified differently for the same data class, compliance risk may emerge.
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data to either agent.
Document data-class handling before deployment.
Set retention defaults explicitly.
Review jurisdictional requirements if scope changes.
